problem: Existing semantic maps (grid, topological, dense geometric) trade off explicit geometry against multi-scale (instance + region) semantics, and store implicit feature tensors that need extra projection/alignment training to be used by LLMs/VLMs/MLLMs.
motivation: ObjectNav, InstNav and SQA all need geometry-aligned instance and region semantics. Large models natively consume text and images, not feature tensors, so a map exposing text plus rendered images would plug into them zero-shot without alignment training.
key_idea: GLMap: a 2D indexing grid over instance and region semantic units, each storing a natural-language description plus 3D Gaussians (built analytically by a Gaussian Estimator) that can be rendered into images for LLM/VLM/MLLM reasoning.
insight: Text and rendered images are directly consumable by large models, so plugging GLMap into ESC, VLFM, ApexNAV and GPT4Scene improves all of them without training (e.g. ESC SR +9.6, VLFM +6.6 on HM3D). The ablation on HM3D shows instance-only (57.4 SR) and region-only (56.2) each beat the VLFM baseline (52.5), and both together give 59.1, so the two semantic scales are complementary.
method: GLMap structure: M={2D grid m, instance units (Gaussians+text), region units (instance IDs+text)}; the grid stores IDs of the units projected into each cell for spatial queries

Gaussian Estimator: voxelizes the instance point cloud (1 cm voxels) and fits mean and covariance analytically over each voxel's Chebyshev-1 neighborhood, using mean color and fixed opacity 0.8, with no gradient optimization

Curvature-aware merging: Gaussians are merged when D(Gi,Gj) (mean, Frobenius covariance, color distances) is below a threshold scaled by a curvature proxy, keeping more Gaussians on curved regions and fewer on flat ones

Incremental update: Gemma3-27B parses each RGB frame into instances and regions; GroundingDINO+MobileSAM give masks, which are back-projected to point clouds; instances are matched by text embedding cosine >0.8 (nomic-embed-text) plus Gaussian mergeability; regions are matched by text similarity plus shared instances; long text is merged by Qwen3-8B

Navigation with GLMap: an LLM or VLM scores each unit against the goal text (VLM scores rendered Gaussian images); scores are Gaussian-smoothed on the grid into a value map; the frontier nearest the max-value cell becomes the waypoint, and FMM does local planning

SQA with GLMap: an LLM estimates region-near-agent and instance-faced probabilities to localize agent position and heading; 4 directional views are rendered with 3DGS and fed with the question to an MLLM

setting.backbone: Gemma3-27B (frozen MLLM for semantic parsing) + GroundingDINO + MobileSAM + nomic-embed-text + Qwen3-8B (merging); plugs into ESC/VLFM/ApexNAV/GPT4Scene
setting.action_space: discrete: move_forward, turn_left, turn_right, stop; frontier waypoints with FMM local planner
setting.simulator: Habitat (HM3D, MP3D); SQA3D on ScanNet scenes
setting.privileged: none (SQA uses provided RGB-D video frames, intrinsics and poses)

numbers.extra: training-free; the 62.7/33.7 row is the ApexNAV+GLMap entry in Tab. 2
numbers.evidence: Tab. ObjectNav: GLMap (Ours) HM3D SR 62.7, SPL 33.7; Tab. LLMs: ApexNAV+GLMap 62.7/33.7
Tab. ObjectNav: GLMap (Ours) MP3D SR 42.5, SPL 18.3

numbers.extra: follows PSL/UniGoal setting; text-described instance goals
no alignment training; the paper does not name the split

numbers_note: Splits are not stated in the paper; the ObjectNav and InstNav 'val' and SQA3D 'test' labels are assumed defaults. The HM3D-ObjNav main row appears to correspond to ApexNAV+GLMap.
results: GLMap gets 62.7 SR / 33.7 SPL on HM3D and 42.5 / 18.3 on MP3D ObjectNav, beating BeliefMapNav (61.4 SR on HM3D) and ApexNAV (59.6). It reaches 22.5 SR on InstNav (vs UniGoal 20.2) and 58.5 EM-1 on SQA3D (vs GPT4Scene 57.2), and adds gains to ESC, VLFM, ApexNAV and GPT4Scene.
limitations: Depends on a large MLLM (Gemma3-27B) plus GroundingDINO/MobileSAM per frame, so compute and latency are high and errors in descriptions or masks propagate
Evaluated only in simulation; no real-robot tests, and the gains over strong baselines are modest (e.g. +3.1 SR for ApexNAV, +1.3 EM-1 for GPT4Scene)
Region units store no Gaussians and rely on instance-level grounding, so unrecognized structure may be missed
